rv.q: Jeremy Herrin is bang on the money with his revival of this much less familiar piece from 1974.
The result is a fine blend of the comic and the painful.
Full of amusing gaffes that demonstrate our nervousness aboutdeath, the play is weakened by a back story that does not, to my mind, add up and by the steroetypical nature of the characters.

cn.t: Ayckbourn's 1974 tragicomedy receives a sharp revival that balances laughter and tears. Critics praise the production's ability to find humor in grief while capturing the play's timeless psychological insights.
